reason: Reproduced by driving master.html?v=approach&state=owner-editing in Chromium and diffing painted pixels, not computed styles. b.css:812 .b-seg sets overflow:hidden; its two buttons are 37px tall inside a 39px plate (1px border each side), so the top, bottom and outer edges of the button box coincide with the plate's padding box. shell.css:311 draws :focus-visible as outline:2px solid var(--focus) at outline-offset:2px, i.e. a rectangle 2-4px OUTSIDE the button box, which the plate's clip removes. Tabbing (real Tab presses, :focus-visible confirmed true, computed outline 2px solid rgb(255,255,255) offset 2px on both buttons) and pixel-diffing the plate region against the unfocused baseline: at 390x844 and 768x1024 the plate is exactly full-bleed and focusing HIDDEN changes ZERO pixels - no focus indicator of any kind on a keyboard tab stop; focusing SHOWN changes 74 pixels, a single 2x37 white stripe at its right edge, which lands on the divider between the two buttons and reads as a thickened rule, not as focus. At 1440 the plate is wider than its buttons, so each button gets one orphan 2x37 stripe (74px changed) sitting to its right; still no ring, and for Shown the stripe is ambiguous between the two controls. Neither gate covers this: interaction-check.mjs:105-114 focuses document.querySelector('button, a[href], [tabindex], input') - one element, the bar's first .b-act, not in the editor - and returns true on parseFloat(outlineWidth) > 0, which a fully clipped outline satisfies; audit.mjs only reads outlineWidth/outlineStyle for contrast eligibility. lessons.md has no entry for this. Not taste, not a gate restatement, not a constraint breach: the two controls that decide what a guest sees are a WCAG 2.4.7 failure on phone and tablet. The finding overstates one detail - at 1440 a 2px stripe does change - but its substance holds at every width and is total at 390/768. Fix verified by injecting it: with .b-seg overflow:visible and the corner clip moved to the children, both buttons paint a full ring (Shown 483px changed, bbox 78x45; Hidden 418px, bbox 80x45) at 390, 768 and 1440, and the unfocused plate is pixel-identical to the current build (0 pixels differ), so nothing about its shape changes.
sharpenedFix: In b.css:812 drop overflow:hidden from .b-seg and move the corner clip to the children: .b-seg button:first-child { border-radius: 5px 0 0 5px } and .b-seg button:last-child { border-radius: 0 5px 5px 0 } - 5px is the plate's 6px minus its 1px border, so the pressed fill still meets the border cleanly and the at-rest render is byte-identical (measured). Prefer this over outline-offset:-2px, which the file already uses at b.css:736 for .b-edit: an inset ring on a 37px button with a white pressed fill would sit on top of the fill and vanish on the pressed side, which is exactly the second failure mode below. Then replace interaction-check.mjs:105-114 with a painted-pixel assertion, since a declared outline proves nothing: for every visible focusable element in every state, screenshot the element's box expanded by outline-offset + outline-width before and after a real keyboard focus, and fail if the two images are identical OR if the changed pixels' bounding box does not extend beyond the element's own border box. The second clause is what catches a ring that survives the clip but paints the same colour as the fill it lands on - the exact reason focusing Hidden at 390 today changes nothing at all.
